name: Olympic (Port Angeles)
tagline: Rainforest, glaciers and wild coast in one park
summary: Port Angeles is the harbour town gateway to Olympic National Park, which packs three worlds together. Drive up to Hurricane Ridge for glacier views, walk the mossy Hall of Mosses in the Hoh Rain Forest, swim in Lake Crescent, and explore sea stacks and tide pools on Rialto and Ruby beaches.
seasonNote: July to September is driest; the coast and rainforest are wet most of the year.
arrival: Seattle–Tacoma International is about 2.5 hours by car and ferry; the Coho ferry links to Victoria, Canada.
gettingAround: A car is essential; the park has no internal roads linking its sides.
cashTip: Cards and tap-to-pay work everywhere; tip 18 to 20 percent at restaurants. Sales tax is added at the till.
foodTip: Dungeness crab, smoked salmon and Pacific oysters.
buyTip: Lavender from nearby Sequim and local smoked fish.
baseArea: Port Angeles, Lake Crescent or Forks

connections.note: Drive with the Bainbridge or Kingston ferry.
